findings.text: the fragment states every class lands below 1e-6 at every step, but its own receipt gives 2.45e-6 (cut), 2.69e-6 (whole), 4.77e-6 (axis) and 2.65e-6 (random) at relative step 1e-7, and the headline at line 13 saying 1e-7 to 1e-9 is two decades below that maximum, so the record's accept verdict rests on numbers it contradicts.

the done-when requires the certificate state beside the stalled one, but titan2/mismatch.json holds one state and titan2/measure.log stops at the stalled STATE line, so half the required comparison, its table and its half of the figure are absent.

the gate log titan2/measure.log has no EXIT= line because the run died before this echo, so the gate status is unread; and its revision header reads 869f1fd81 while the POSITIVE_CONTROL line it carries is produced by code first added in 1af9c7e75, so the log cannot be tied to the reviewed head.

positive_control computes its own quotient as matrix @ plus minus matrix @ minus and never calls the fresh_cd construction at measure.py:250, so the negation and step-scale defects it claims to guard would have passed it.

the term split switches only the booking and moving-geometry contributions, leaving the bank operator, edge intervals, boundary and axis flux and current normalisation that the brief names never individually differentiated.
the fragment closes an article tag it never opens, which breaks the composed record's markup.
each panel is titled inline where the figure caption is meant to carry that identity, and the stalled series is drawn in red, which the style reserves for a limit being broken.

status reads complete while the checkpoint on the same line says the certificate half is the only remaining work, and tests names a direct measure.py invocation where the log header records run_h200.sh, so the recorded gate cannot be re-run as written.
the done-when specifies one H200 and the sole measurement ran on a Tesla P100 (titan job 1308028); the receipt discloses the device, but the evidence does not meet the done-when's own wording.
